function: Construction of fine-grained channel fingerprints (channel-power maps, i.e. channel knowledge maps) by x4 super-resolution of coarse maps, to support CSI acquisition in massive MIMO (p. 1, 3).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM: BS with 8x8 UPA, single-antenna users, 2.4 GHz, 15 kHz subcarrier spacing, 128 m x 128 m area; no RIS (p. 11, Table I).
method: Conditional denoising diffusion model (U-Net with self-attention) trained supervised on coarse/fine map pairs; one-shot layer pruning with multi-objective knowledge distillation gives a lightweight version (pp. 5-10).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa v2.6.1 with 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS; 6,000 simulated coarse/fine channel-power map pairs with random BS positions, split 5:1 into training and testing (p. 11).
test_conditions: Train and test on x4 maps (32x32 to 128x128) from the same QuaDRiGa data; zero-shot test on x16, x8, x2 magnification without retraining (pp. 11, 13).
baselines: Learned only: SRGAN-MSE, SRGAN, C-VAE, DRRN super-resolution networks trained the same way; no non-learned (interpolation) baseline in Tables II-III (p. 13).
metrics: NMSE, MSE, PSNR and SSIM between reconstructed and ground-truth channel-power maps (p. 11, Tables II-III).
complexity: FLOPs and parameters swept over hyperparameters (Fig. 6); default CGDM 221.21 M parameters and 54.58 GFLOPs; pruning algorithm time O(nU/s+nC) (pp. 10, 12-13).
openness: none (no code or data link; data generated with QuaDRiGa) (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 10: "The ground-truth channels are generated using the widely adopted QuaDRiGa generator (version 2.6.1)"; p. 11: "3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS".
q2_support: p. 13: "the neural network learns and updates its weights solely on the ×4 SR CF dataset, without exposure to the ×16, ×8, and ×2 SR CF datasets".
q3_support: p. 13: "we compare them with several state-of-the-art models, including SRGAN-MSE [21], SRGAN [21], C-VAE [26], and DRRN [37]". All four are learned; Tables II-III hold no non-learned method, and interpolation appears only in Remark 1 (p. 4) without comparison.
q4_support: p. 13: "parameter count of 221.21 M and FLOPs of 54.58 G".
q5_support: p. 11: "by running QuaDRiGa simulations with different BS locations". The data are self-generated; no code or data link or DOI appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included under area 2: the learned function is x4 super-resolution of channel knowledge maps (channel power), framed as CSI acquisition for massive MIMO (p. 1); reviewer to confirm that this counts as channel synthesis or prediction and not as an excluded radio-map function. q2 rests on zero-shot tests at other magnification factors (p. 13) on the same QuaDRiGa data, not on a new propagation scenario.
